paragraphs.source_en: The ethnographic record may be useful to the interpretation of the Round Head painted sites since there is no reason to exclude that regular meetings of Central Saharan foragers existed in the Early Holocene times. Meetings between neighbouring groups were certainly necessary at least to ensure reproduction, since marriages had to be probably arranged outside the group, as suggested by the ethnographic record (Lee 1979). Evidence for the inter-regional contacts may be identified in two ways. Firstly, in the pottery which has the same decoration across the Sahara and secondly in the extraordinary stylistic unity of the Round Head paintings and in the same elements characteristic for this artistic tradition. Such similarities may either confirm the same cultural base of all Central Saharan groups or frequent contacts between them.

paragraphs.source_en: In this hypothesis, the Tassili Plateau may have possibly been a special place for meetings. The highest concentration of the Round Head paintings there would testify a rather intense frequentation and the character of the images, namely masks, body decorations and dances among others, could suggest ritualistic or solemn occasions. The Plateau and especially the painted sites could have been sacred areas where groups, dispersed across a large territory during the year, united in certain selected periods. On the Plateau the paintings are accumulated in two main sites, namely Sefar and Jabbaren containing hundreds of images, with other minor sites distributed around them. The territory around the Plateau (the northern part of the Tassili, the Algerian Tadrart and the Tadrart Acacus) presents minor painted sites or isolated shelters with a few images.

paragraphs.source_en: Some shelters located in narrow wadies, surrounded by rocks or in a high position where the access is difficult, do not permit to large groups to enter and usually only a few persons can stay there at a time. What could have been the function of these minor sites? The ethnographic record suggests various uses for the local painted shelters.
